vectors.enisa_quote: Exfiltration can be conducted over alternative protocols and web services
vectors.reason: ENISA names no site; 'web services' and automated export run in ground IT and Annex C lists 'Ground: SLE/SDL protocols', so a foothold in ground systems is the best-supported origin.

rows.enisa_quote: Exfiltration of sensitive satellite data, resuliting in a data breach
rows.reason: Siphoning stored and streaming mission data out of ground systems, with automated bulk export, is the data breach and the 'web services' channel ENISA states.

rows.enisa_quote: Exfiltration can be conducted over alternative protocols and web services
rows.sparta_quote: provide discreet avenues to move data off the spacecraft
rows.reason: Covert use of a secondary link is the spacecraft-side analogue of exfiltration over an alternative protocol; judgement call, since ENISA wording is IT-oriented.

rows.enisa_quote: Exfiltration can be conducted over alternative protocols and web services
rows.sparta_quote: so the spacecraft emits mission data over paths the program does not monitor or control
rows.reason: Retuning or remapping the link so that data leaves in a non-standard form is exfiltration over an alternative protocol on the radio side.

rows.enisa_quote: Exfiltration can be conducted over alternative protocols and web services
rows.sparta_quote: add a low-rate subcarrier under the main modulation
rows.reason: Adding a subcarrier or new waveform in a software-defined radio is an alternative protocol in the most literal sense.

rows.enisa_quote: Exfiltration can be conducted over alternative protocols and web services
rows.sparta_quote: forwarded outside the planned ground segment
rows.reason: Remapping a transponder so selected channels leave toward other receivers is exfiltration over a different path.
A foothold in the ground systems is where data are staged and exported and where the automation runs.
